problem: The GCC name is explained as 'arm-none-eabi-gcc', where 'none' is said to mean 'no operating system'. In the standard machine-vendor-OS triplet, 'none' fills the vendor slot (no vendor), and the absence of an OS is shown by 'eabi' standing in for an OS name such as 'linux'. A student can carry the wrong field meaning into an exam answer.
fix: Write: 'arm' is the target architecture, 'none' is the vendor field (no vendor), and 'eabi' in place of an OS name means bare-metal code using the Embedded Application Binary Interface.

problem: The chapter says .text holds 'code and constants'. Read-only constants are normally placed in a separate .rodata section, which the linker script then puts in flash alongside .text. Calling .text the home of constants is loose and can mislead a student reading a real map file.
fix: Write: '.text for code, .rodata for read-only constants (both usually placed in flash), .data for initialised variables, and .bss for zero-initialised variables.'

problem: The cross-reference 'See Chapter 6.3 for that trade-off' is plain text, while other chapters are meant to be linked so a phone reader can jump to them.
fix: Use a chapter link, for example: See Chapter 6.3 for that trade-off.
